labels.rationale: Usage question: stripping markup from a string is supported via Text.from_markup(...).plain.

body:
This looks like a usage question. Rich can strip markup from a string: parse it with `Text.from_markup()` and read `.plain`, which has the tags removed:

```python
from rich.text import Text

plain = Text.from_markup("[bold red]Apple[/] pie").plain  # "Apple pie"
```

If the text may contain literal square brackets, escape them with `rich.markup.escape()` first. See the [markup docs](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/blob/master/docs/source/markup.rst). Related: #2016. For usage questions, [Discussions](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/discussions) is the right place.
